blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: The received superscriptions associate psalms with David, Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, Heman, and Ethan and also preserve genre, performance, tune, instrument, and narrated-setting labels. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

A literary feature to notice is that The Masoretic Psalter contains 150 psalms arranged in five books, with doxological boundaries after Psalms 41, 72, 89, and 106 and a final crescendo of praise in Psalms 146-150. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. Interpretations differ on some details.
